big_story.headline: BSE ENTERS NIFTY
big_story.subhead: BSE JOINS THE BENCHMARK INDEX AS WIPRO EXITS IN MAJOR REJIG
paragraphs: The benchmark Nifty has undergone a major rejig with BSE officially joining the elite index while Wipro exits. Indian shares are reacting to shifting market dynamics as oil comes off its highs. Investors are closely monitoring how index weightages and structural changes impact overall portfolio allocations.

Index reconstitutions often trigger massive institutional rebalancing, compelling passive funds to adjust their holdings accordingly. Such shifts highlight the evolving prominence of exchange operators and financial infrastructure within India's capital markets. Analysts point out that inclusion in premier benchmarks brings heightened visibility and liquidity.

Market participants must navigate these structural changes while keeping an eye on broader macroeconomic indicators. As trading progresses, the inclusion of BSE alongside other index movements will shape institutional strategies. Understanding these portfolio shifts is essential for anyone tracking Dalal Street.
big_story.pullbox: Index reconstitutions trigger massive institutional rebalancing as BSE joins the Nifty while Wipro exits.

explains.title: What is an Index Rejig?
paragraphs: An index rejig or reconstitution is the periodic review of a stock market index to ensure its constituents accurately reflect the broader market. Index providers add growing companies and remove underperforming or shrinking ones based on strict liquidity and market capitalization criteria.

When a prominent stock enters an index like the Nifty, institutional funds tracking that benchmark must automatically buy its shares. This dynamic often influences trading volumes and short-term price movements across Dalal Street.

Paediatric health-tech startup Primerry has successfully raised ₹7.1 crore in a fresh pre-seed funding round. The capital injection will enable the young enterprise to expand its specialised pediatric healthcare products and services across the market.

Early-stage venture backing allows innovative startups in niche sectors like pediatric health-tech to scale their operations rapidly. This funding milestone highlights growing investor appetite for technology-driven healthcare solutions tailored for families.

story_1.headline: Sun Pharma Plans ₹10,000 Cr Bond Sale for Refinancing
paragraphs: Sun Pharma is planning to raise ₹10,000 crore through a rupee bond sale to refinance its loan for the Organon acquisition. The pharmaceutical major aims to restructure its debt portfolio following the deal. The transaction marks one of the largest corporate bond issuances by an Indian healthcare company this fiscal year.

Market watchers note that the bond sale will help lower borrowing costs and extend debt maturity. Investors are closely monitoring the company's capital allocation strategy as it consolidates its international operations.

story_2.headline: Jaishankar Outlines Friction Points in India-US Trade Deal
paragraphs: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has highlighted key factors delaying the trade agreement between India and the United States. He noted that an ongoing US trade investigation under Section 301 poses challenges to concluding negotiations smoothly.

Despite hurdles, Jaishankar emphasized that a trade deal, if concluded, could significantly improve bilateral economic relations. Both nations continue talks to resolve regulatory concerns and trade friction.

story_3.headline: YouTube Creator Economy Delivers ₹18,000 Cr GDP Boost
paragraphs: YouTube's creator ecosystem in India has generated an economic impact of over ₹18,000 crore on national GDP while supporting 9.6 lakh jobs. Meanwhile, Union Minister of State L. Murugan emphasized that future AI developments should empower digital creators rather than compete against them.

geopolitics.headline: India-EU Free Trade Deal Moves Toward Finalisation
paragraphs: The India-EU Free Trade Agreement is moving toward finalisation, marking a landmark deal for both economies. According to the new EU envoy, Paquet, this free trade deal sends a strong signal that rules-based commerce still matters in the global economy. Manuel Muñiz also highlighted India's rising global significance, stating that missing India means missing a large chunk of the 21st century.

As negotiations progress, the finalisation of this landmark deal represents a major step forward for bilateral commerce. For Indian businesses and markets, a successful agreement will open up new avenues for trade and investment with European partners. However, both sides must navigate the final stages of talks to ensure the agreement delivers on its promise of rules-based commerce.
